name: Loop against block game
purpose: Points where one player opens with a loop and the other blocks. Learn to win with the loop and to survive with the block.

variants.instructions: One player serves short backspin; the other pushes long. The server loops, the receiver blocks, play it out. Games to 7, then swap.
The feeder sends one long backspin, then blocks anything you loop. Play it out like a point: 7 points, count wins.
variants.feederInstructions: First ball long backspin, then block every loop back to a random spot.

variants.instructions: Robot: one backspin, then topspin to random spots. Loop the first, then keep looping or block. Count how many 4-ball sequences you finish.

coachingPoints: Blocker: stay close, bat in front
After the loop, get ready for the block

name: Open-up game
purpose: Push until a ball is long enough, then be the first to open with topspin from either wing.

variants.instructions: Serve backspin. Push until a ball comes long, then open with topspin. A point won by the first opening counts 2. Games to 11.
The feeder pushes 2 to 4 balls, then one long to a random side. Push the short ones, open the long one.
variants.feederInstructions: Backspin pushes; every few balls, one long to a random side.

variants.instructions: Robot on backspin to random spots. Push the short balls, open the long ones with topspin.

name: Counter-loop points
purpose: Points that start with a loop: the receiver must counter-loop or block, then play on.

variants.instructions: Your partner serves, you push long, they loop, you counter-loop. Play it out. Games to 7, then swap.
Robot on heavy topspin to random sides, stand back. Counter-loop and count sets of 4 counter-loops on the table.

name: Flick the receive
purpose: Receive short serves with a flick to take the initiative.

variants.instructions: Your partner serves short anywhere. Flick every serve you can; push the ones you can't. Play the point out. 10 serves, then swap.
The feeder serves short to random spots. Flick each serve.
variants.feederInstructions: Serve short with varied spin from your end, random placement.

coachingPoints: Flick to the corners or the elbow

name: Finish the point
purpose: When you get a high ball, finish it. When you are under attack, lob and fight back.

variants.instructions: Each point starts with one player hitting a high ball. The other smashes; play it out. 10 points, then swap.
The feeder mixes normal balls and high balls. Drive the normal ones, smash the high ones. Count smash winners.
variants.feederInstructions: Mostly normal topspin; every 3–4 balls, a high one.

coachingPoints: Aim wide, away from the lobber

name: Chop and attack
purpose: Defend with chops until you get a weak ball, then attack it. The chopper's game in one drill.

variants.instructions: Your partner attacks with loops; you chop. When a ball sits up, attack it. Games to 11.
Programmable robot: 4–6 topspin balls to random sides, then one high or short ball. Chop the topspin, attack the last ball.

coachingPoints: Vary the backspin: heavy, then light

name: Pressure points
purpose: Practise closing out tight games: every game starts at 8–8 or 9–9.

variants.instructions: Play games that start at 8–8. Use your pre-point routine before every point. Best of 5 games.
Robot on random. Each set of 5 balls is a 'point': all 5 on the table wins it. First to 3 points; start every set with your routine.
Rebound board up. A 'point' is 10 balls in a row. Start at 8–8 against an imaginary opponent: miss and they score.
The feeder plays random balls; each 4-ball sequence is a point. Start at 8–8.
variants.feederInstructions: Random placement, a little faster than normal.

coachingPoints: Play your normal shots, just with more margin

name: Handicap games
purpose: Close games with a stronger or weaker partner: the stronger one starts behind.

variants.instructions: Play to 11. The stronger player starts at 0, the other at 3–5 (agree on it). Change the start after each game so it stays close.

coachingPoints: Pick one thing to try each game

name: Robot match simulation
purpose: Random balls with no pattern, like a match. Read, move, decide.

variants.instructions: Robot on random placement and mixed spin. Each 6-ball set is a 'point': 5 of 6 on the table wins it. Play to 11.
Rebound board up. Hit to different spots on the board on purpose: left, right, middle. A 'point' is 8 good balls in a row. Play to 11.
The feeder plays random balls with mixed spin. Each 6-ball set is a 'point'.
variants.feederInstructions: No pattern: mix placement, length and spin.

name: Serve and receive points
purpose: Short points that start with a real serve and receive: the first three balls decide most points.

variants.instructions: Each player serves 5 in a row. Play every point out as in a match. A point won within the first 4 balls counts 2. Games to 11.

coachingPoints: Serve with a plan for ball three

name: Up and down the table
purpose: A fun pressure game: win to stay on, lose and you swap.

variants.instructions: Play single points. Each point you win is a step 'up'. First to 5 steps in a row wins the round. A lost point sends you back to 0.

coachingPoints: Every point is a fresh start
Play safe on big points, not passive
